title: Negotiation Sandbox: Liability Fallback, Escrow Preview & Contract Risk Simulation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Negotiation Sandbox tool that lets sales, PMs, and legal preview the downstream product and pricing impacts of common MSA/DPA redlines. The sandbox will compute an estimated operational cost delta (tokens, reserved capacity impact), SLA/regret exposure, and generate a recommended escalation path including an indemnity/limitation-of-liability fallback tier and escrow requirements. It will integrate template clauses, scored risk heuristics, and a simulated timeline for legal review cycles. The goal is to enable faster, consistent triage of redlines during pricing/packaging experiments and enterprise contract negotiations.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive UI prototype exists showing clause toggles and live estimated cost + latency SLO impact for a representative set of product routes
Backend service computes a redline risk score (0-100) with factors: indemnity cap, data residency, SLA deviation, escrow demand, and third-party subprocesses
Automated recommendation produced: allow | escalate to legal | auto-decline, with explicit rationale and suggested contract language
Integration links to: PRD in Confluence, a GitHub feature branch with a mock API, and a demo dashboard recording simulated negotiation flows
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales Ops, Legal (Corporate), and Product by end of Cycle 2026-W10
success_metrics: Reduce avg legal review turnaround for standard MSA/DPA redlines from 9 business days to <= 3 days for auto-recommended cases
Increase self-serve redline closures by Sales from 12% to 50% for low-risk deals during pricing experiments
Surface expected unit-cost impact on deal pricing within 5% accuracy for 85% of simulated scenarios
notes_and_updates: 2026-02-13: Kickoff with Legal and Sales Ops. Agreed heuristics for risk score buckets: Low (<=30), Medium (31-65), High (>65).
2026-02-20: Prototype wireframes reviewed by Design. Feedback: make liability cap slider discrete (tiers) and show explicit downstream runtime implications per tier.

2026-02-28: Engineering spike completed to estimate token-cost delta for three common routes (chat-struct, completion, embeddings). Results included a delta model and simple lookup table for prototype.
2026-03-05: Legal requested explicit escrow clause language variants for US/EU customers. Added to clause library; flagged country-specific fallback in heuristic logic.
2026-03-09: Sales pilot with two AE teams scheduled for 2026-03-16. Pilot will use sandbox during pricing experiments for 20 deals.
2026-03-12: Decision to scope Phase 1 to read-only sandbox + recommendations; full writable clause export and auto-populate into contract templates deferred to Phase 2 due to security review.
Follow-ups assigned: Marco to own API contract; Priya (Legal) to draft final clause variants; Elena (Sales Ops) to coordinate pilot AEs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect cost model gives misleading pricing guidance -> Mitigation: conservative buffers in Phase 1, transparent confidence interval on estimates
Risk: Automated recommendations cause legal exposure -> Mitigation: require explicit legal sign-off for any escalate-to-approve recommendations and mark auto-recommendations as advisory
Risk: Country-specific data/residency rules are complex -> Mitigation: white-list known regulated countries and surface manual review for those territories
tradeoffs: Full automation vs conservative guardrails: we prioritize safety and audit trail over speed for Phase 1
Accuracy vs complexity: initial cost model uses heuristics and lookup tables instead of full runtime simulation to ship faster
UI scope: prioritize clarity for Sales rather than exposing internal risk-scoring math
open_questions: What threshold of risk_score should trigger mandatory legal review for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity?
How to surface indemnity caps in deals where customers request custom SLAs beyond our standard product tiers?
Should escrow requests automatically convert to reserve chargebacks in pricing experiments or be treated as non-monetary operational constraints?
